title: Module 13 Interpretation Check
intro: Each item gives you a short research situation. Decide what the evidence supports.

items.q: A researcher finds r = .41 between hours of sleep and a memory score for 30 students. The critical r for df = 28 at alpha = .05 two-tailed is .361. What is the decision?
o: Reject the null. The correlation is significant
Retain the null. The correlation is weak
Reject the null. The correlation proves sleep improves memory
items.why: The obtained r of .41 exceeds .361. A significant correlation still does not show causation.

items.q: What proportion of memory score variability does sleep account for in that sample?
A new anxiety scale produces the same scores for the same people when given two weeks apart (r = .90). Which type of reliability is this?
items.why: The same measure is given at two times.

items.q: A scale reliably gives consistent scores but correlates poorly with other accepted anxiety measures. What is the problem?
o: Weak validity. It is consistent but may not measure anxiety
items.why: Convergent validity is shown by correlating with other measures of the same construct.

items.q: Two raters score the same 40 essays. Their scores correlate at r = .85. This supports
items.why: Agreement between independent raters is interrater reliability.
